topic: Weak-event honest inference for probabilities of necessary and sufficient causation under ignorability, monotonicity, and overlap: construct a rare-event-calibrated confidence set by inverting the cross-fitted orthogonal PN/PS ratio score over triangular arrays whose factual conditioning-event probability d_n may vanish; derive uniform coverage from explicit nuisance-rate and score-moment conditions, recover Tian-Wu's efficient Gaussian limit when n d_n diverges, and prove the matching minimax expected-diameter frontier min{1,(n d_n)^(-1/2)} with a nonshrinking Poisson boundary at n d_n=O(1); use Hannart-Naveau rare-event climate PN/FAR and Tian-Wu stroke attribution as applied consumers.

open_problems.open_problem: Can an inverted cross-fitted orthogonal score deliver uniformly valid confidence sets for PN and PS over triangular arrays in which the relevant factual conditioning-event probability d_n may vanish, including the Poisson-to-Gaussian transition?

source_refs.claim: The paper writes PN as a ratio with factual-event denominator E[AY], uses cross-fitting and fixed-law nuisance-product conditions, and proves efficient Gaussian inference without a vanishing-denominator sequence.
source_refs.author: Zhaoqing Tian and Peng Wu

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that a familiar normal-approximation binomial interval does not have uniform asymptotic coverage, demonstrating the boundary failure that rare-event calibration must avoid.
source_refs.author: Longcheen Huwang

source_refs.excerpt: insert e(X)-weighted versions of pi1, nu_L, nu_U, the EIFs, and the one-step estimators
the cross-fitted one-step CLT was not discharged from the declared primitive nuisance and sampling assumptions

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tian and Wu's efficient theory is a regular fixed-law result, while a weak-event sequence makes the PN/PS ratio influence function and its studentization depend on d_n and turns the validation-fold event count from asymptotically Gaussian to Poisson when n d_n is bounded. The adjacent CausalSmith PoC run also exposed a mismatch between treated-event ratio formulas and their EIF implementation and could not discharge its cross-fitted CLT from primitive assumptions. Ordinary Wald calibration is therefore not uniform, but classical exact rare-binomial intervals do not accommodate learned causal nuisances or orthogonal-score remainder terms.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform-coverage theorem for a fully specified inverted orthogonal PN/PS ratio score, with explicit triangular-array nuisance-rate and score-moment assumptions, a Poisson or exact-count boundary law for n d_n=O(1), and Tian-Wu's efficient Gaussian limit when n d_n tends to infinity.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact PN/PS definitions, identifying assumptions, efficient-score benchmark, and stroke-attribution application that the weak-event result should extend.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PN and PS formalize causal attribution -> ignorability plus monotonicity identifies them as observed-law ratios -> efficient influence functions give regular Gaussian inference -> what inference remains honest when the conditioning event becomes rare?

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitting and Neyman-orthogonal score expansion to isolate nuisance-product drift, then rescale each remainder by the weak event's effective standard deviation rather than by a fixed root-n norm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired statistic is a learned-nuisance orthogonal score, but its validation law and remainder scale vary with d_n.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt identification-robust test inversion and a feasible variance estimator whose size remains uniform as the information-bearing first-stage component weakens.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require inverting a score whose identifying denominator can be weak, so validity must not depend on a regular Wald expansion.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over rare-binomial coverage diagnostics and effective-count calibration across exact and Gaussian proportion intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After orthogonalization, the remaining regime switch is driven by the same vanishing Bernoulli event count, although the causal score adds nuisance drift.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the minimax expected diameter of an honest confidence set for a bounded PN/PS ratio of order min{1,(n d_n)^(-1/2)}, with unavoidable nonshrinking diameter when n d_n remains bounded?

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes semiparametric efficiency at regular laws but does not give a minimax confidence-set diameter theory indexed by a shrinking PN/PS conditioning-event probability.
source_refs.author: Zhaoqing Tian and Peng Wu

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that identification through arbitrarily thin sets can destroy regular root-n estimation and make the attainable rate depend on relative support tails.
source_refs.author: Shakeeb Khan and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: The paper proves that ratio-like weak-information models can preclude confidence sets having both positive confidence and finite expected diameter, anchoring the zero-information boundary phenomenon.
source_refs.author: Leon Jay Gleser and Jiunn T. Hwang

source_refs.excerpt: leaves the exact weak-overlap minimax rate open
needs a shell-matching converse — a minimax lower bound at the R_n^* rate

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular semiparametric efficiency bounds describe only the n d_n to infinity regime, and generic weak-identification impossibility results do not exploit that PN and PS are bounded in [0,1]. The failed CausalSmith weak-overlap run similarly had an estimator-side envelope and a parametric floor but no class-uniform shell-matching converse off the root-n regime. Closing the proposed frontier requires a bounded-parameter least-favorable experiment that separates two PN/PS values using only the rare conditioning stratum and a matching upper confidence set that retains uniform coverage with zero or finitely many events.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching minimax upper and lower expected-diameter bounds of order min{1,(n d_n)^(-1/2)}, including a two-point or fuzzy-hypothesis Poisson-experiment lower bound proving constant diameter when n d_n=O(1) and an attaining honest score-inversion procedure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its identification-versus-estimability narrative makes the effective information loss from a thin conditioning event immediate before specializing to bounded PN/PS targets.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal ratio may remain point identified -> its information can reside on sets of probability d_n -> regular root-n inference fails as those sets thin -> what is the sharp honest-diameter frontier as a function of n d_n?

method_exemplars.technique: Localize a fuzzy-hypothesis lower-bound construction to perturbations supported on the rare conditioning stratum and calculate both causal-ratio separation and experiment distance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required converse is a causal-functional minimax lower bound whose effective sample size is n d_n.

method_exemplars.technique: Use convergence toward a zero-information ratio experiment to force positive probability of large confidence-set diameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical expected-diameter impossibility argument for a ratio whose denominator becomes uninformative.

method_exemplars.technique: Define minimax expected length under honest coverage and match testing lower bounds to an adaptive interval construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the exact decision-theoretic expected-length template needed to turn a point-risk rate into an honest confidence-set diameter theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: Which primitive nuisance-rate, localization, and score-moment conditions are sufficient, and nearly necessary, for the cross-fitted PN/PS orthogonal score to recover Tian-Wu's efficient Gaussian limit uniformly whenever n d_n diverges?

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies the target efficient influence functions and regular large-sample benchmark, but not triangular-array conditions tracking a diverging ratio-score norm as d_n decreases.
source_refs.author: Zhaoqing Tian and Peng Wu

source_refs.claim: The paper proves root-n Gaussian inference for low-dimensional causal parameters with learned nuisances using Neyman orthogonality and cross-fitting under fixed regularity and moment conditions.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Mert Demirer, Esther Duflo, Christian Hansen, Whitney Newey, and James Robins

source_refs.claim: The paper gives honest inference for global and shrinking-local regression functionals using regularized Riesz representers, but not the PN/PS ratio score or its rare-event normalization.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Whitney Newey, and Rahul Singh

source_refs.excerpt: replacing Assumption frontier-active with a primitive lower-bound construction
an empirical-process upper bound for localized report classes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Standard DML rate products are calibrated to a fixed score variance, whereas the PN/PS ratio score has a representer or influence norm that grows as d_n shrinks. Thus an o_P(n^-1/2) unnormalized remainder may still dominate the effective (n d_n)^-1/2 fluctuation, and fixed L2 or q-moment hypotheses need not yield a uniform Lyapunov or self-normalization bound. The prior DML-frontier proposal explicitly left primitive lower constructions and localized empirical-process bounds open, so neither it nor the published local-Riesz theory states the nuisance-product, entropy, and score-tail frontier for this causal ratio.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem and matching local-alternative counterexample that express Gaussian recovery in explicit d_n-scaled nuisance-product rates, foldwise localization norms, entropy bounds, and uniform score moments, and that reduce to Tian-Wu's semiparametric variance and limit law when d_n is bounded away from zero.

writing_exemplar.why: Its efficiency derivation is the benchmark to preserve, so the new narrative should pivot directly from regular efficiency to the missing triangular-array regularity frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PN/PS admit efficient influence functions -> cross-fitted nuisance learning can target those scores -> a rare conditioning event inflates the score norm and remainder scale -> which primitive conditions still recover the efficient Gaussian law?

method_exemplars.technique: Track a growing Riesz-representer norm through orthogonal bias bounds, empirical variance consistency, and uniform Gaussian approximation for shrinking-local targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A weak-event ratio is a local functional whose effective representer norm diverges, even though its causal target remains bounded.

method_exemplars.technique: Threshold unstable inverse-weight contributions, expose black-box nuisance-rate costs, and prove studentized asymptotic normality under weak overlap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It explicitly recalibrates doubly robust causal t-statistics when the usual semiparametric variance and nuisance-rate bookkeeping become unstable.

method_exemplars.technique: Use conditional-on-training fold decompositions to separate empirical score noise from second-order nuisance drift without Donsker assumptions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the base proof architecture that must be made uniform in d_n rather than replaced.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one obtain honest rare-event confidence sets for climate PN/FAR after the event threshold or multivariate projection has been selected to maximize causal evidence, rather than treated as fixed in advance?

source_refs.claim: The paper converts a climate trajectory into an event occurrence by maximizing causal evidence and presents PN/FAR as especially relevant for extreme events, creating a data-adaptive rare-event target.
source_refs.author: Alexis Hannart and Philippe Naveau

source_refs.claim: The paper models multivariate climate extremes with generalized Pareto laws and selects an optimal linear projection to maximize probabilities of causation, while its inference is tied to the parametric extreme-value construction.
source_refs.author: Anna Kiriliouk and Philippe Naveau

source_refs.claim: The review emphasizes that extreme-event attribution depends on rare factual and counterfactual probabilities and surveys inference and modeling assumptions without a selection-honest PN confidence-set theorem.
source_refs.author: Philippe Naveau, Alexis Hannart, and Aurelien Ribes
source_refs.venue: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application

open_problems.why_unsolved: Climate attribution deliberately searches over thresholds, trajectories, or projections to strengthen PN, but the same search changes the conditioning event and its probability and can select an unusually favorable rare-event ratio. Fixed-threshold delta-method or generalized-Pareto inference omits this optimization step, while generic post-selection methods do not account for cross-world causal nuisance estimation and the Poisson boundary when the selected factual exceedance count is small.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform post-selection coverage theorem for a confidence set indexed over an admissible threshold or projection class, with simultaneous orthogonal-score calibration, explicit complexity conditions, and rare-event critical values that remain valid for the selected PN/FAR target.

writing_exemplar.why: Its bridge from extreme-event attribution to Pearl-style PN and its causal-evidence optimization are the exact applied motivation to mirror.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Climate attribution compares factual and counterfactual event risks -> PN/FAR gives a causal reading for an observed extreme -> analysts choose the event definition to maximize causal evidence -> how can uncertainty remain honest after that rare-event search?

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse multivariate peaks-over-threshold likelihood, tail-dependence estimation, and projection optimization, but embed them in a simultaneous rather than fixed-projection confidence procedure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the actual rare-climate PN estimator and optimization map whose selection effect must be covered.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt precision-corrected supremum inference, Gaussian-process approximation, and inequality selection to a threshold/projection-indexed orthogonal PN score.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The selected attribution target is an extremum over an indexed family, so simultaneous control must precede optimization.

literature_map:
Tian and Wu (2025, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2407.10185, doi:10.1002/sim.70242) derive PN/PS EIFs, cross-fitted ratio estimators, and regular Gaussian efficiency.
Their PN denominator is the factual-event probability E[AY], but their fixed-law product-rate and large-sample theory does not formulate a vanishing-denominator triangular array.
Pearl (1999) and Tian and Pearl (2000) anchor identification and bounds for probabilities of causation; they do not supply weak-event inference.
Hannart and Naveau (2018, Journal of Climate, doi:10.1175/JCLI-D-17-0304.1) interpret climate PN as FAR and choose event definitions to maximize causal evidence.
Kiriliouk and Naveau (2020, AOAS, arXiv:1908.03107) estimate PN for multivariate extremes with generalized Pareto models and optimize a linear projection.
Naveau, Hannart, and Ribes (2020, Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application) survey rare-event attribution inference and the sensitivity of factual/counterfactual tail risks.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) provide the cross-fitting and Neyman-orthogonality template under regular score scaling.
Chernozhukov, Newey, and Singh (2022, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1802.08667) treat shrinking-local functionals with learned Riesz representers, but not causal probability ratios at a Poisson boundary.
Dorn (2025, arXiv:2504.13273) proves thresholded doubly robust Gaussian inference under weak overlap and makes nuisance-rate costs explicit.
Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA7372) show that information concentrated on thin sets yields irregular, support-tail-dependent rates.
Kaji (2021, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA16413) supplies a general weak semiparametric identification framework and impossibility results, but not a bounded PN/PS diameter frontier.
Mikusheva and Sun (2022, ReStud, doi:10.1093/restud/rdab097) demonstrate uniform test inversion and feasible variance estimation under weak information in IV models.
Chen (1990, JASA), Huwang (1995, Statistics & Probability Letters), and Bai and Lam (2025, Journal of Applied Probability, arXiv:2305.02434) show why rare-binomial Gaussian calibration is not uniformly reliable at small effective counts.
Gleser and Hwang (1987, Annals of Statistics, doi:10.1214/aos/1176350597) anchor finite-expected-diameter impossibility for ratio-like zero-information models.
The live tensions are regular PN/PS efficiency versus vanishing conditioning events, orthogonal nuisance learning versus diverging score norms, Gaussian approximation versus bounded Poisson counts, and honest coverage versus sharp expected diameter and data-adaptive climate event selection.
